references.text: Moses and Aaron bowed down and worshiped when the Lord revealed himself to the people of Israel, a similar act of worship in God's presence.
The people bowed down and worshiped when they heard about the Lord's salvation, the same expression of reverence and worship.
Abraham's servant bowed to the ground and worshiped the Lord, the same physical expression of worship shown by Moses.
Abraham's servant bowed to the ground before the Lord, a parallel act of humble worship.
Balaam bowed down and fell on his face when he saw the angel of the Lord, a similar response of awe in God's presence.
The people worshiped at the entrance of their tents when they saw the pillar of cloud, the context for Moses' meeting with God.
The twenty-four elders fall down and worship him who sits on the throne, a New Testament parallel to worship in God's presence.
The elders fell down and worshiped, the same attitude of deep reverence that Moses showed.
A parallel to Moses' humble response (falling on his face) as a reaction to God's presence or judgment.
